description: Slack mrkdwn formatting reference. Slack uses mrkdwn, NOT standard Markdown. Key differences: *bold* (not **bold**), _italic_ (not *italic*), <url|text> (not [text](url)).

rules.name: bold
rules.description: Bold text. Note: standard Markdown uses **text** for bold, but Slack uses single asterisks.

rules.name: italic
rules.description: Italic text. Note: in standard Markdown *text* means italic, but in Slack *text* means bold. Use underscores for italic.

rules.name: strikethrough
rules.description: Strikethrough text. Standard Markdown uses ~~text~~ (double tilde), Slack uses single tilde.

rules.name: inline-code
rules.description: Inline code. Same as standard Markdown. Text inside will not use any other formatting.

rules.name: code-block
rules.description: Multi-line code block. Do NOT include a language hint after the opening backticks — Slack does not support syntax highlighting and will render the language name as code.

rules.name: blockquote
rules.description: Block quote. Prefix each quoted line with >. Each consecutive quoted line needs its own > prefix.

rules.name: link
rules.description: Named link. Standard Markdown uses [text](url) but Slack uses angle brackets with a pipe separator. Plain URLs are auto-linked.

rules.name: email-link
rules.description: Email link. Must use mailto: prefix.

rules.name: line-break
rules.description: Newline. Use the literal string \n in API-submitted text.

rules.name: unordered-list
rules.description: Simulated bullet list. Slack has no native list syntax. Use the bullet character (•) with newlines.
rules.example: • Item one\n• Item two\n• Item three

rules.name: emoji
rules.description: Emoji in colon format. Unicode emoji are also supported and auto-converted to colon format.

rules.name: date
rules.description: Dynamic date formatting. Renders dates in the viewer's local timezone. Tokens: {date_num}, {date}, {date_short}, {date_long}, {date_pretty}, {time}, {time_secs}, {ago}.

mentions.name: user-mention
mentions.description: Mention a user by their Slack user ID (e.g. U012AB3CD). Do NOT use @username — it renders as plain text. Use resolve_user_id to look up the ID from a name.

mentions.name: channel-link
mentions.description: Link to a channel by its ID (e.g. C012AB3CD). Do NOT use #channel-name — it may not link. Use get_channel_id_by_name to look up the ID.

mentions.name: user-group-mention
mentions.description: Mention a user group by ID. The literal string !subteam^ is required before the group ID.

mentions.name: here
mentions.description: Notify active members of the channel. Use sparingly.

mentions.name: channel-notify
mentions.description: Notify ALL members of the channel, active or not.

mentions.name: everyone
mentions.description: Notify everyone in #general. Most disruptive — use with extreme care.

escaping.description: Ampersand must be escaped as HTML entity
Less-than must be escaped as HTML entity
Greater-than must be escaped when used as literal text (not for blockquotes or link syntax)

unsupported.note: Not supported in mrkdwn. Use *bold text* on its own line, or header blocks in Block Kit.
Not supported in mrkdwn. Use image blocks in Block Kit.
Not supported in mrkdwn. Use code blocks for tabular data or rich_text blocks.
No native support. Simulate with numbered text and newlines: 1. item\n2. item
Not supported in mrkdwn. Use divider blocks in Block Kit.
Nested inline formatting is not reliably supported.
Does NOT work. Use *text* instead (single asterisks).
Language hints are NOT supported. The language name will be rendered as part of the code. Use plain ``` with no language.
